authority: Artifact identity is the OBJECT stored at consumer_artifact_commit (blob sha256, or the LFS pointer oid with its payload verified separately), not the working-tree file. Metadata records are read and parsed from the resolved metadata commit and must equal the working tree. Hashing the current file would let a later edit be attributed to an earlier commit.

rebuilds.method: two clean detached git worktrees checked out at the consumer source commit

role_definitions.candidate_metadata_commit: descends from artifact; contains CANDIDATE.json, READINESS.json, LINEAGE.json, PROVENANCE.json
role_definitions.consumer_artifact_commit: descends from source; contains the canonical AAB, APK and VERIFY.json
role_definitions.consumer_source_commit: contains every input used to build the candidate and none of the artifacts

roles.candidate_metadata_commit: auto — resolved by `git log -1 --format=%H -- releases/aurelius/candidates/2.0.0-rc2/CANDIDATE.json`; a metadata file cannot contain its own commit hash

superseded_roles.note: The rc2 artifacts did not change. These earlier roles are kept for history: the source commit moved when the build.gradle.kts comment was corrected and the artifact commit moved when VERIFY.json gained the debug-dex classification. A rebuild from the new source commit reproduces the identical artifact hashes.

verify: python3 tools/verify_lineage.py aurelius --version 2.0.0-rc2 --source f6f00663f109490e294b0c0d60d1e224087c3dd0 --artifact fa995ffad97c260ffb64a77d4f0916b593eb66a5 --metadata auto --build
why_this_matters: rc1 recorded a single consumer_commit (399ba12) that PREDATED the packaging work which produced its artifacts. Ancestry alone would only prove ordering; rebuilding from the declared source commit and matching the canonical bytes proves the attribution is true.
